How to debone a chicken - The best method I've found thus far

Difference there is that he isn't actually deboning the entire thing. He is parting it up, which is useful. But if you're making a gillete/roll type thing, then it's kind of useless.

My favorite chicken roast is to have the full chicken deboned, add a stuffing of chorizo sausage with apricot, and then rolling it up, no bones. Its very fun to do, and carves amazingly.
I've never considered mixing chorizo with apricot; How does it taste? Does it mix well with other fruits?

It does have to be dried apricot, because it has less of a 'fresh sweet' taste, and more of a subtle taste. It was quite excellent when minced together in a small food processor. I do like fruits paired with meat, so I didn't mind this at all. It did need a bit of seasoning, salt, pepper, but the chorizo did a lot of the flavoring. I think it was about a 1:2 mix of the sausage with the fruit. Anything added would have been too much, and the consistency was lovely.

I always also season the inside of the bird before I prepare the stuffing to let it rest with it.
It sounds delicious. I'll have to try it as soon as I can manage to get the deboning down. I take it when you say minced you mean both the chorizo and apricot together?

Yeah, honestly chopping it up finely will suffice, but I find making more of a mince helps it become a spreadable stuffing a lot easier. It had the consistency of a dry, chunky chutney.

The deboning is quite easy. Even on the first try, I got all the bones out. I think the hardest part was making sure the wish bone was broken without smashing my hand on the chopping board. After that it's just cutting through those joints and getting rid of the sinew.
Oh man, it looks so delicious! And he makes it seem so easy :)

Seriously, it is. I've done 5 chickens with this method so far. The first time I took my time and didn't go as fast, getting my SO to pause and unpause it every step, but it was worth it to get the technique.
Mhh interesting, it surely would be a first-timer for me. Do you have any recipes you'd recommend with a deboned chicken like this?

For this one? Basically debone the chicken (except for the legs or wings if you enjoy eating off the bone like that... it can add a little flavour), and lay it upside down. Then add a hot stuffing you enjoy. I've used spinach and mushroom (nicely flavoured with various spices), apricot and chorizo, and one time I just used an entire small wheel of Camembert.

Then, roll it up, roast at 190C until the thickest part of the meat is 75C or it looks cooked (I really just go by eye unless its super thick).

I also add an egg wash on the skin to make it super crunchy, maybe adding a complimentary herb rub. Also chuck in some potatos and make a salad to go with it.
Man, you're giving me ideas for this weekend... thanks! I'll add it to my list :)
You just gave me a foodgasam reading that.

Its so good man, you can basically mix 2 of your favorite flavours and end up with an amazing basic stuffing. None of this "Bread crumbs and MSG" shit, give me something decent any day.

I do recommend a hot stuffing for most poultry if you ever do a stuffing on a chicken or turkey, boned or not. Otherwise it takes WAY too long to cook and ends up dry and horrible. Most people just buy the store stuffing (which isn't always bad), but its cold so it takes too long to heat up the middle of the chicken. A hot stuffing helps cook the chicken from the inside out.
